predecessors.name: Antigonid kingdom (Macedon)
predecessors.text: Thessaly, which 'had been part of the Macedonian kingdom continuously since 353 BC' and which Macedonia gave up in the peace of 196

successors.name: Roman Republic
successors.text: Thessaly, from which the Romans disbanded the leagues in 146 BCE and which the Macedonia page counts among the lands originally in the province of Macedonia

ledger.x: 196: the new koinon is a Roman-protected federation.

c. 185: the occupied towns are returned. No page opened dates this (antigonid-dynasty places the surrender c. 185 on the usual account); the Second Macedonian War page has Thessaly Macedonian 'continuously since 353 BC' only up to 197.
146: Rome ends the league's protection by dissolving it.

wars.name: Roman-Seleucid War
wars.outcome: The Macedonians entered the war against the Aetolians in spring 191 and occupied Thessalian towns; Antiochus lost the war after Thermopylae (191) and Magnesia ad Sipylum (December 190).

wars.name: Third Macedonian War
wars.outcome: The first clash was 'an inconclusive battle at Callinicus in 171 BC'; Rome won at Pydna in 168; no Thessalian border change is on the page.

certainty.note: No page gives the League's frontier; Thessaly is the region between Epirus, Macedon, Phocis and the Aegean, with the Magnesian coast uncertain.
